Path to Genius — A Concept-Level, Dependency-Ordered Self-Study DAG

Proof-level rigor across 41 subjects + a parallel competitive-programming track. Ordered as a prerequisite DAG (Phase 0 → 4), not subject-by-subject. Every node = one atomic concept with a source pointer and ← requires / → enables links. Each section header carries the single best lecturer/course beyond the textbook + the assignment set to actually produce work. Multi-year; not a race.

Progress saves in this browser automatically. To see it on every device you travel with, connect a private GitHub Gist. Your token is stored only in this browser — it is never written into the page on GitHub.


Same token on each device → same progress everywhere. Lost a device? Revoke the token in GitHub settings; its blast radius is limited to your gists.

Links are canonical pointers chosen for stability: MIT OpenCourseWare course pages (with course numbers + assignment tabs), cp-algorithms.com per-algorithm pages, course homepages, and named textbook section/theorem references. Not every URL was individually live-checked; the named course + section still locates the material if a link moves. Nothing fabricated.
Build track (do, don't just read) — the forcing function a reading list lacks:
1. Nand2Tetris — build a working computer from NAND gates → CPU → assembler → VM → OS → compiler.
2. CMU 15-213 CSAPP labs — bomb, attack, cache, malloc, shell. Reading H&P ≠ building a memory system.
3. Onur Mutlu DDCA / 18-447 labs — pipelined → out-of-order core, cache & DRAM simulators. (Your day job, leveled up.)
Pair these with the architecture, OS, and PL sections below.

THE TRACK — 20 threads that cut across every subject

Subject boundaries are an administrative artifact, and keeping them as the study order is what stops you seeing that the material is one thing. The 41 sections further down stay as the reference substrate — where a concept lives and what it requires. These 20 threads are the study order. Each follows a single idea through every subject it appears in and ends in something you ship. A thread's list is the complete prerequisite closure of its payoff, ordered nearest-the-payoff-first: when you reach any item, this plan has already taught you everything it depends on. The subject tag on the right is deliberate — a normal session runs Rudin → Strang → Herlihy, and the point is that those are one argument in three costumes.
